effect: Ciprofloxacin may increase the anticoagulant effect of oral anticoagulants including warfarin.
mechanism: The label says the contribution of ciprofloxacin to increased INR is difficult to assess and can vary with infection age and general status.
guidance: The cited label recommends frequent prothrombin time and INR monitoring during and shortly after co-administration. Medication changes require a prescriber or anticoagulation clinician.
limitation: Applies to co-administration with an oral anticoagulant; this tool cannot estimate an individual INR or bleeding risk.

effect: Tetracyclines may increase anticoagulant effect in patients receiving anticoagulant therapy.
mechanism: The doxycycline label states that tetracyclines can depress plasma prothrombin activity.
guidance: The cited label notes that anticoagulant dosage may require clinician adjustment. Do not change either medicine without the treating clinician.
limitation: The label describes the tetracycline class and does not quantify an individual effect size or timing window.

effect: Thyroid hormone can increase the anticoagulant activity of oral anticoagulants.
mechanism: The label describes increased catabolism of vitamin K-dependent clotting factors with impaired compensatory clotting-factor synthesis.
guidance: The cited label recommends careful prothrombin time monitoring and clinician-directed anticoagulant adjustment.
limitation: Applies to oral anticoagulants; effect depends on thyroid status and therapy changes and is not a same-dose timing rule.
